Bone marrow contains many stem cells. Some of these stem cells are responsible for the replacement of red blood cells.
During the production of red blood cells a series of changes occur to the cell structure.

Fig. 5.2 shows the production of a red blood cell from one of these stem cells.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
People who travel to high altitude become acclimatised to the conditions.

Athletes often train at high altitude before competing at sea level.

A group of male and female athletes who trained at sea level moved to high altitude for further training. Sports scientists analysed blood samples taken from the athletes to measure any changes in the concentration of haemoglobin in the blood and changes in the haematocrit.

Haematocrit is the volume of red blood cells expressed as a percentage of the total volume of a sample of blood.

The results are shown in Table 5.1.

Table 5.1

| feature of the blood | at sea level | after 19 days at high altitude | percentage increase |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| mean concentration of haemoglobin in the blood $/ \text{g }100\text{cm}^{-3}$ | 13.3 | 15.1 |  |
| mean haematocrit | 41.0 | 42.5 | 3.7 |
parts.text: Complete Table 5.1 by calculating the percentage increase in haemoglobin concentration.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why it is necessary for the athletes to increase the concentration of haemoglobin in their blood when acclimatising to high altitude.
